_comment: Phase 0 scaffold. The six named cultures below are palette + theme stubs; furniture/outfit/ship/station art is borrowed from the graphics_pipeline_test story (design-JSON pipeline - see docs/GRAPHICS_PIPELINE.md). Real per-culture assets land in Phase 6.1-6.6 - see docs/PLAN.md. orbital_std / regolith_std are kept only so the borrowed pipeline building_types keep resolving their culture colours; remove them once every system has its own.

harbor_authority.name: The Harbor Authority
harbor_authority.description: Descendants of the Relay's original traffic controllers, around the yellow star Halcyon. They kept their records, their uniforms, and their conviction that they are the rightful centre of a civilisation that no longer exists. Polite, bureaucratic, quietly desperate to matter again.
harbor_authority.theme: Authority architecture is orderly, symmetrical, and over-signed: clean rectangular halls, evenly ranked windows, a painted deck grid, chrome-and-navy livery, and a docking-guidance chevron on every surface that could carry one. Pull hull/wall from metal_color, glass/light from glass_color, thrust from thrust_color. It should read as a institution that has kept its uniform pressed for 200 years with nobody left to inspect it.
harbor_authority.naming: PLACES: Relay-era designations kept verbatim - 'Halcyon Approach', 'Beacon 1', 'Hub Control', 'Sector Green'. PEOPLE: '<given> <surname>', measured and vaguely nautical (Harbor-Master Ellis Crane, Controller Vane, Signalwoman Doss). Titles are traffic-control ranks: Controller, Harbor-Master, Signal Officer, Approach Warden.

ninefold_combine.name: The Ninefold Combine
ninefold_combine.description: A guild-state in the red-dwarf system Kiln, where every person belongs to a trade lineage and a contract is sacred to the point of religion. They survived the Silence by rationing everything and enforcing it without mercy. They do not want the Relay back.
ninefold_combine.theme: Combine work is heavy, dark iron banded with ember-orange hazard light, built for the deep mines: low vaulted volumes, blast doors, riveted seams, ration-stencil numerals on every bulkhead. Odd counts and ornament are waste. Pull hull/wall from metal_color, hazard glow from glass_color, thrust from thrust_color. It should feel like a place where warmth and air are metered.
ninefold_combine.naming: PLACES: a mine designation plus a lineage - 'Kiln', 'Ninefold Deep', 'Shaft VII', 'Combine Hold'. PEOPLE: '<given> <lineage>-<trade>' compressed to '<given> <surname>' in speech (Vess Tol676-Cutter, spoken 'Vess Tolcutter'). Titles are guild ranks: Factor, Warden of Contract, Deepmaster, Tallykeeper.

the_drift.name: The Drift
the_drift.description: The people of Verdance's single cloud-city and its ring of agricultural habitats. They run on rolling consensus, hold no fixed hierarchy, and distrust anyone who gives orders. The most welcoming system in the region and the least able to actually decide anything.
the_drift.theme: Drift structures are soft, rounded, and planted: curved partitions, trellised light, growing things worked into every wall, pale timber-and-canvas tones over a green cast. Nothing is load-bearing that could instead be woven. Pull hull/wall from metal_color, grow-light from glass_color, thrust from thrust_color. It should feel improvised by committee and quietly alive.
the_drift.naming: PLACES: gentle descriptive compounds - 'Verdance', 'Highcanopy', 'the Undergarden', 'Ring Nine'. PEOPLE: a single given name, or given plus a habitat ('Sela of Highcanopy'). No inherited titles; functional ones only, lowercase in feel: speaker-for-now, water-keeper, seed-warden.

the_vigil.name: The Vigil
the_vigil.description: A monastic order of a few hundred in the dead Ossuary system, who stayed behind to keep the graves and the archives of everyone the first decades of the Silence killed. They hold the truest history in the region, and believe the Relay went dark on purpose - to contain something.
the_vigil.theme: Vigil spaces are austere and vertical: long cold halls, name-walls, narrow light, unpolished grey stone and violet-white glass, no decoration that is not a record. Pull hull/wall from metal_color, lamp/glass from glass_color, thrust from thrust_color. It should feel like a library that is also a tomb.
the_vigil.naming: PLACES: memorial designations - 'Ossuary', 'the Name-Wall', 'Vault of the First Decade', 'the Long Vigil'. PEOPLE: a taken single name, often archaic (Keeper Aramis, Sister Vane, the Archivist). Titles: Keeper, Archivist, Warden of Names, the Vigil-Master.

the_wardens.name: The Wardens
the_wardens.description: Not a government but a maintenance cult grown up on the ringworld fragment at the old network core, operating Relay-era machinery they no longer understand. The reactivation signal originates here.
the_wardens.theme: Warden space is ancient monumental engineering with a scavenged priesthood living in its margins: vast smooth Relay-era forms in dark alloy and teal light, patched with mismatched salvage and hand-lettered ritual markings. Pull the monumental shell from metal_color and glass_color, the salvage from the free_carrier palette, thrust from thrust_color.
the_wardens.naming: PLACES: Relay-core designations worn into liturgy - 'the Span', 'Hub Zero', 'the Core Choir', 'Ring Segment 4'. PEOPLE: a rank-name, the given name mostly lost (First Warden, Warden of the Fourth Segment, the Signal-Tender). Titles: Warden, Signal-Tender, Keeper of the Hub.

free_carrier.name: Free Carriers
free_carrier.description: Independent traders and salvagers who have run slow-boat routes between the isolated systems for generations. The Relay's fast lanes returning is either their golden age or the end of their livelihood.
free_carrier.theme: Carrier ships and berths are patchwork: mismatched hull segments from six cultures welded into one working whole, cargo lashing everywhere, hand-painted names. No unified livery - that is the livery. Pull the base from metal_color, running lights from glass_color, thrust from thrust_color, and freely borrow one panel each from the other cultures' metal_colors.
free_carrier.naming: PLACES: carriers don't own places; they name berths after themselves ('Ferro's Slip'). PEOPLE: '<given> <surname>', polyglot and worn (Nix Ferro, Dume Halloran, Captain Ash). Titles are shipboard only: Captain, Mate, Super, Wrench.

orbital_std.description: Borrowed from graphics_pipeline_test so the pipeline station/furniture art resolves its culture colours. Remove in Phase 6.
